questionSections.title: Group B - Q4: Answer the following questions

items.answer: Data communication is the process of exchanging data or information between two or more devices through a transmission medium.
items.solution: Two modes of data communication: Simplex mode (data flows in one direction only) and Half-duplex mode (data flows in both directions, but only one at a time). Full-duplex (both directions simultaneously) is also an acceptable third mode.

items.answer: Antivirus software is a program designed to detect, prevent, and remove malicious software such as viruses, worms, and trojans from a computer system.
items.solution: Two examples: Avast Antivirus and Quick Heal Antivirus (Norton, McAfee, and Kaspersky are also acceptable).

items.answer: Software security refers to the protection of software and the data it processes from unauthorized access, misuse, or damage, typically using measures such as antivirus programs, passwords, and firewalls.
items.solution: Two measures of hardware security: (1) Keep computer hardware in a locked/secure room to prevent theft or unauthorized physical access. (2) Use an Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) and voltage stabilizers to protect hardware from power fluctuations and damage.

items.answer: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a network of physical devices, vehicles, appliances, and other objects embedded with sensors and software that lets them connect to the internet and exchange data with each other.
items.solution: Two importances of IoT: (1) It automates everyday tasks, making homes and workplaces more efficient and convenient (e.g. smart home devices). (2) It enables real-time monitoring and data collection, which is useful in fields like healthcare, agriculture, and traffic management.

items.answer: E-commerce is the buying and selling of goods and services, or the transfer of funds or data, over an electronic network such as the internet.
items.solution: Types of e-commerce: Business-to-Business (B2B), Business-to-Consumer (B2C), Consumer-to-Consumer (C2C), and Consumer-to-Business (C2B).

items.answer: A table is a database object that stores data in an organized structure of rows (records) and columns (fields).
items.solution: Design View is used to modify a table (its field names, data types, and properties).

items.answer: A query is a database object used to retrieve, filter, or manipulate data stored in tables based on specified criteria.
items.solution: Two importances of query: (1) It allows quick retrieval of specific data from large tables based on given conditions. (2) It can be used to update, delete, or summarize data automatically, saving manual effort.

items.answer: Validation Rule is a condition/expression set on a field that data must satisfy before it can be entered, while Validation Text is the custom error message displayed when entered data violates that Validation Rule.
items.solution: Example: a Validation Rule of '>0' on a marks field would only accept positive numbers, and its Validation Text might say 'Marks must be greater than 0' when an invalid value is entered.

items.answer: A Form is used for entering, viewing, and editing data conveniently, while a Report is used for presenting and printing data in a formatted, read-only layout.

rows: Mainly used for data entry and editing.
Data displayed can usually be modified.

questionSections.title: Group B - Q5: Dry run the given program

items.answer:
Output (each character printed on its own line):
D
v
l
p
e
t
items.solution: A$ = "Development" (length 11: D-e-v-e-l-o-p-m-e-n-t at positions 1-11). The loop runs C = 1 to 11, STEP 2, so C takes the values 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11. Each time, X$ picks out the character at position C using MID$(A$, C, 1), and since PRINT X$ has no trailing semicolon, each character is printed on its own line. C=1 gives 'D', C=3 gives 'v', C=5 gives 'l', C=7 gives 'p', C=9 gives 'e', C=11 gives 't'.
items.code:
DECLARE SUB Result (A$)
A$="Development"
CALL Result (A$)
END

SUB Result (A$)
FOR C=1 TO LEN(A$) STEP 2
  X$=MID$(A$,C,1)
  PRINT X$
NEXT C
END SUB

questionSections.title: Group B - Q6: Correct the bugs in the given program

items.answer: The program has three bugs: a missing file number in EOF(), an invalid DISPLAY statement, and a mismatched loop-closing keyword.
items.solution: (1) 'DO WHILE NOT EOF( )' is missing the file number argument; it must be 'DO WHILE NOT EOF(1)' to check the end of file #1. (2) 'DISPLAY RN, N$, E, Ne' is not a valid QBASIC statement; it must be 'PRINT RN, N$, E, Ne' to output the record. (3) A loop opened with 'DO WHILE' must be closed with 'LOOP', not 'WEND' ('WEND' only pairs with a plain 'WHILE'); so the closing keyword must be changed to 'LOOP'. 'CLOSE' has also been made specific as 'CLOSE #1' to match the file opened with that number.
items.code:
REM to display records
OPEN "marks.dat" FOR INPUT AS #1
CLS
PRINT "Roll Number", "Name", "English", "Nepali"
DO WHILE NOT EOF(1)
  INPUT #1, RN, N$, E, Ne
  PRINT RN, N$, E, Ne
LOOP
CLOSE #1
END

questionSections.title: Group B - Q7: Study the given program and answer the questions

items.answer: A and B
items.solution: A and B are the formal parameters declared in FUNCTION MUL(A, B); they receive the values of M and N (the actual arguments) when the function is called as MUL(M, N).
items.code:
DECLARE FUNCTION MUL (A, B)
M=5
N=3
PRINT MUL (M,N)
END

FUNCTION MUL (A, B)
  MUL = A*B
END FUNCTION

items.answer: Function procedure
items.solution: The program defines and uses FUNCTION MUL(A, B) ... END FUNCTION, which is a Function procedure - it takes parameters, computes a value (A*B), and returns that value directly to the calling statement PRINT MUL(M,N).

questionSections.title: Group C - Q8: Convert/Calculate as per the instruction

items.solution: Group the 8-bit binary number into sets of 4 bits from the right: 0010 1001. Convert each group: 0010 = 2, 1001 = 9, giving the hexadecimal number (29)16.
In decimal: (111)2 = 7 and (10)2 = 2. First multiply: 7 x 2 = 14 = (1110)2. Then subtract (111)2 = 7: 14 - 7 = 7 = (111)2.
Convert 86 to binary by repeated division by 2: 86=64+16+4+2, which corresponds to binary digits 1010110 (64+0+16+0+4+2+0=86).

items.answer: Quotient = (101)2, Remainder = (1)2
items.solution: (1011)2 in decimal is 11, and (10)2 in decimal is 2. 11 divided by 2 gives a quotient of 5 with a remainder of 1. Converting back: 5 = (101)2 and 1 = (1)2.

questionSections.title: Group C - Q9: Answer the following questions

items.answer: A QBASIC program using a Function procedure for the sum and a Sub procedure for the average, as shown in the code field.
items.solution: The main module takes three numbers A, B, and C as input. It calls the Function procedure Total(A, B, C), which returns A+B+C, and prints the result directly since a function returns a value. It then calls the Sub procedure Average(A, B, C) using CALL, which computes (A+B+C)/3 internally and prints it itself, since a sub does not return a value to the caller.
items.code:
DECLARE FUNCTION Total (A, B, C)
DECLARE SUB Average (A, B, C)

CLS
INPUT "Enter first number: ", A
INPUT "Enter second number: ", B
INPUT "Enter third number: ", C

PRINT "Sum = "; Total(A, B, C)
CALL Average(A, B, C)

END

FUNCTION Total (A, B, C)
    Total = A + B + C
END FUNCTION

SUB Average (A, B, C)
    Avg = (A + B + C) / 3
    PRINT "Average = "; Avg
END SUB

items.answer: A QBASIC program that creates the sequential data file "record.txt" and stores Roll Number, Name, Address, and Class for multiple students, as shown in the code field.
items.solution: The file "record.txt" is opened FOR OUTPUT, which creates it if it does not already exist. A DO...LOOP WHILE loop repeatedly asks the user for a student's Roll Number, Name, Address, and Class, and writes each record to the file using WRITE #1 (which automatically adds quotes around string values and separates all items with commas). After each record, the user is asked whether to add another; the loop continues as long as the answer is "Y". Finally the file is closed.
items.code:
OPEN "record.txt" FOR OUTPUT AS #1
CLS
DO
    INPUT "Enter Roll Number: ", RollNumber
    INPUT "Enter Name: ", Name$
    INPUT "Enter Address: ", Address$
    INPUT "Enter Class: ", Class$
    WRITE #1, RollNumber, Name$, Address$, Class$
    INPUT "Add another record (Y/N): ", Ans$
LOOP WHILE UCASE$(Ans$) = "Y"
CLOSE #1
END

questionSections.title: Group C - Q10: Write a program (attempt either option)

items.answer: A C program that reads a number and reports whether it is odd or even, as shown in the code field.
items.solution: An integer n is read using scanf. The expression n % 2 gives the remainder when n is divided by 2; if this remainder is 0, n is even, otherwise n is odd. An if-else statement prints the appropriate message.

items.answer: A C program that displays the series 2, 4, 6, 8, ... up to 100, as shown in the code field.
items.solution: A for loop starts at i = 2 and runs while i <= 100, increasing i by 2 in each iteration (i = i + 2). Each value of i is printed, producing the series 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, ... up to 100.
